scenes.heading: Notebooks
scenes.narration: A Databricks notebook is an interactive document of runnable cells where you write code, see results, and collaborate in real time.

scenes.heading: Why notebooks
bullets: Cells run independently and in order
Mix Python, SQL, Scala, and R
scenes.narration: Cells let you run pieces of code independently, so you can iterate quickly without rerunning everything. A single notebook can mix Python, SQL, Scala, and R using magic commands. And multiple people can co-edit and comment at once, like a shared document.

scenes.heading: Switching languages with magics
scenes.code:
# Default cell runs Python
df = spark.read.csv('/mnt/raw/sales.csv', header=True)

# %sql magic runs SQL in the next cell
# %sql
# SELECT region, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY region
scenes.narration: Here the default cell reads a CSV into a Spark DataFrame using Python. By placing a percent SQL magic at the top of a cell, the very same notebook can run SQL against your tables. This flexibility lets engineers and analysts collaborate in one place.

scenes.text: Keep notebooks focused and parameterize them so they can be reused in scheduled jobs, not just interactive exploration.
scenes.narration: Keep each notebook focused and parameterized so it can be reused in scheduled jobs, not only for interactive exploration.
